problem.title: Design a Multi-Core Async Task Runtime with Lock-Free Work-Stealing & Cooperative Preemption
problem.tagline: Architect a 64-core async runtime sustaining 2M wakeups/sec using Chase-Lev work-stealing deques, 61-tick fairness, and 128-poll cooperative budgets.
problem.purpose: Design a lock-free multi-core task scheduler with zero false sharing, half-batch stealing, blocking-pool isolation, and sub-microsecond dispatch.

spark.summary: Core-pinned workers combine a 20 ns LIFO slot, 64-byte-padded 256-slot Chase-Lev deques, 61-tick global fairness, and 128-poll cooperative preemption.
spark.keyTakeaway: Pad top/bottom cache lines, steal half-batches with XorShift randomization, cap searching thieves at cores/2, and isolate blocking syscalls.
spark.byteSummary:
Designing an async task runtime (like Tokio, Go's runtime, or Seastar) capable of multiplexing 500,000 concurrent connections and 2M task wakeups/sec across 64 CPU cores requires sub-microsecond local scheduling, zero lock contention, and strict protection against noisy tasks.

The runtime spawns one OS worker thread per core, each owning a **1-slot LIFO Fast-Path** plus a **256-slot Chase-Lev Work-Stealing Deque** (padded to 64-byte cache lines). External wakeups and local queue overflows land in a sharded **Global Injection Queue**, which workers poll every **61 ticks** for fairness. Idle cores run a randomized XorShift **half-batch steal** loop capped at `cores / 2` searching threads before parking on an `epoll`/`io_uring` reactor.

To prevent a single CPU-bound or blocking task from freezing other coroutines, every task poll runs under a **128-poll cooperative budget**, synchronous disk/FFI work is isolated onto a dedicated `spawn_blocking` pool, and >1 ms poll durations trigger immediate runtime telemetry alerts.

learningJourney.title: Sizing 64 Cores, 500K Tasks & Sub-Microsecond Wakeups
learningJourney.purpose: Define 64-core worker sizing, 2M wakeups/sec throughput, and <500 ns local dispatch budgets.

explanation.foundation: Target 64 CPU cores handling 500K concurrent async tasks and 2M task wakeups/sec with `<500 ns` local schedule latency.
explanation.core: Each of the 64 workers allocates a 256-slot pointer ring (~2 KB) plus a 1-slot LIFO fast-slot—keeping hot scheduler state inside L1 cache.
explanation.deepDive: A lock-free hierarchical timer wheel per worker (or shared sharded wheel) drives RPC deadlines without global lock contention.

learningJourney.title: LIFO Fast-Slot + 256-Slot Deque + Global Queue + epoll/io_uring
learningJourney.purpose: Wire the 3-tier task pickup order (Global/61 -> LIFO Slot -> Local Deque -> Half-Steal -> Park) with the I/O reactor.

explanation.foundation: Each worker loop follows a strict priority order: check Global Injection Queue every 61 ticks, pop LIFO slot, pop Local Deque, else steal half from a random peer.
explanation.core: When all queues are empty, the worker parks on the **epoll / io_uring I/O Reactor** (or a futex) until a socket becomes readable or a new task wakes it.
explanation.deepDive: The LIFO fast-slot handles request-response coroutine ping-ponging in ~20 ns without touching the 256-slot deque.

sectionDiagram.title: LIFO Fast-Slot + 256-Slot Deque + Global Queue + epoll/io_uring

cards.label: LIFO Slot Caveat
cards.detail: Bound consecutive LIFO-slot hops (or count against the 61-tick counter) so two chatty tasks can't starve the deque.

cards.label: I/O Driver Integration
cards.detail: One worker polls epoll/io_uring non-blocking on each tick or when no CPU work remains.

cards.label: External Spawns
cards.detail: Non-worker threads push into the sharded Global Injection Queue and unpark 1 idle worker.

learningJourney.title: 61-Tick Fairness Loop & Half-Batch Steal Scheduler
learningJourney.purpose: Implement the worker event loop with 61-tick global polling, randomized half-steal, and budget-capped task execution.

explanation.foundation: Ensure every worker advances its monotonic tick counter cleanly and never drops tasks during steal or overflow.
explanation.deepDive: Checking `global_q` both at `tick % 61 == 0` AND as a fallback after stealing ensures external submissions never sit idle when workers are free.

sectionDiagram.title: 61-Tick Fairness Loop & Half-Batch Steal Scheduler

cards.label: Zero Lost Wakeups
cards.detail: Falling back to global_q after _try_steal_half() guarantees external tasks are picked up before parking.

cards.label: Atomic LIFO Swap
cards.detail: Clearing lifo_slot before polling prevents re-entrancy loops.

cards.label: Randomized Peer Order
cards.detail: Start victim scan at a random offset to avoid core-0 steal storms.

sectionDiagram.summary: Combining 61-tick global checks, LIFO fast-slots, and steal-then-global fallbacks guarantees progress and low latency.
sectionDiagram.caption: Combining 61-tick global checks, LIFO fast-slots, and steal-then-global fallbacks guarantees progress and low latency.

learningJourney.title: 64-Byte Cache-Line Padding, NUMA Affinity & Sharded Global Queues
learningJourney.purpose: Eliminate false sharing on top/bottom indices and scale global injection queues across 64 cores.

explanation.foundation: If `top` and `bottom` sit in the same 64-byte cache line, every owner push invalidates a thief's read of `top` (false sharing).
explanation.core: Align `top` and `bottom` to separate 64-byte cache lines (`alignas(64)`). For 64+ cores, shard the Global Injection Queue across NUMA nodes or use a lock-free MPSC queue so external spawns don't contend on one mutex.
explanation.deepDive: Pin worker threads to NUMA-local cores and prefer stealing from same-NUMA-socket peers before crossing the QPI/UPI interconnect.

sectionDiagram.title: 64-Byte Cache-Line Padding, NUMA Affinity & Sharded Global Queues

cards.label: False-Sharing Fix
cards.detail: 64-byte padding can boost multi-core work-stealing throughput by 2-3x under heavy stealing.

cards.label: NUMA-Aware Victims
cards.detail: Stealing from same-socket cores first preserves L3 cache locality.

cards.label: MPSC Global Queue
cards.detail: Lock-free intrusive MPSC queues let I/O threads inject thousands of woken tasks without mutex stalls.

sectionDiagram.summary: 64-byte index padding, NUMA-first stealing, and MPSC global queues keep scaling linear up to 64+ cores.
sectionDiagram.caption: 64-byte index padding, NUMA-first stealing, and MPSC global queues keep scaling linear up to 64+ cores.

learningJourney.title: 128-Poll Cooperative Budgets & Blocking-Pool Isolation
learningJourney.purpose: Stop tight async loops and accidental synchronous I/O from starving sibling tasks on the same worker core.

explanation.foundation: An async task reading from a perpetually ready socket (`while stream.ready()`) can monopolize a worker core indefinitely.
explanation.core: Assign each task poll slice a **128-operation cooperative budget**: once exhausted, `Pending` is returned and the task re-queues at the back. Route blocking syscalls (`fsync`, `bcrypt`, `DNS`) to a separate `spawn_blocking` thread pool.
explanation.deepDive: In Go-style runtimes, a background `sysmon` thread detects workers stuck in syscalls >10 ms and hands their local `P` deque to a fresh OS thread.

sectionDiagram.title: 128-Poll Cooperative Budgets & Blocking-Pool Isolation

cards.label: Cooperative Preemption
cards.detail: 128-poll budgets guarantee one noisy socket never starves 10,000 other connections on that core.

cards.label: Dedicated Blocking Pool
cards.detail: Keep bounded blocking thread pools (e.g., max 512 threads) separate from the 64 async workers.

cards.label: Sysmon Handoff
cards.detail: Detaching stalled worker queues prevents FFI/disk stalls from freezing queued coroutines.

sectionDiagram.summary: 128-poll cooperative budgets, spawn_blocking pools, and sysmon queue handoffs isolate noisy and blocking tasks.
sectionDiagram.caption: 128-poll cooperative budgets, spawn_blocking pools, and sysmon queue handoffs isolate noisy and blocking tasks.

learningJourney.title: Panic Isolation, Cancellation Propagation & Graceful Runtime Drain
learningJourney.purpose: Catch task panics without crashing the worker thread and drain in-flight tasks cleanly on SIGTERM.

explanation.foundation: An unhandled panic inside one task must not kill the worker thread and orphan 8,000 other tasks.
explanation.core: Wrap every `task.poll()` in `catch_unwind` (recording the error on the task's `JoinHandle`), and propagate structured cancellation tokens so dropped futures release sockets and locks immediately.
explanation.deepDive: On runtime shutdown, stop accepting new external spawns, signal cancellation tokens, and wait up to a bounded grace timeout for active tasks to drop cleanly.

sectionDiagram.title: Panic Isolation, Cancellation Propagation & Graceful Runtime Drain

cards.label: Worker Thread Survival
cards.detail: Task panics fail only that task's JoinHandle, keeping the worker core and its deque alive.

cards.label: Structured Cancellation
cards.detail: Dropping cancelled futures runs RAII destructors to close file descriptors and release semaphores.

cards.label: Bounded Shutdown
cards.detail: Force-drop stalled background tasks after shutdown_timeout so deploys never hang.

sectionDiagram.summary: catch_unwind panic boundaries and structured cancellation keep worker threads alive and shutdowns bounded.
sectionDiagram.caption: catch_unwind panic boundaries and structured cancellation keep worker threads alive and shutdowns bounded.

learningJourney.title: Tracking Poll Latency Histograms, Steal Counts & Searching Spikes
learningJourney.purpose: Detect accidental blocking inside async tasks, excessive steal thrashing, and global queue backlogs.

explanation.foundation: The #1 production issue in async runtimes is someone accidentally calling a blocking mutex or `requests.get()` on a worker thread.
explanation.deepDive: Page or log slow-poll stack traces whenever any single `poll()` exceeds 2 ms so developers fix blocking code immediately.

sectionDiagram.title: Tracking Poll Latency Histograms, Steal Counts & Searching Spikes

cards.label: 2 ms Slow-Poll Canary
cards.detail: Healthy async polls finish in <50 us; >2 ms polls almost always mean accidental blocking I/O.

cards.label: Forced-Yield Spike
cards.detail: Rising 128-poll budget yields flag CPU-bound loops that belong on a compute pool.

cards.label: Global Queue Alert
cards.detail: Alert if global_queue_depth grows monotonically while worker CPU is <50%.

sectionDiagram.summary: Slow-poll >2 ms stack sampling and forced-yield counters surface hidden blocking bugs before tail latency degrades.
sectionDiagram.caption: Slow-poll >2 ms stack sampling and forced-yield counters surface hidden blocking bugs before tail latency degrades.

knowledgeChecks.question: On a 64-core server, 63 idle workers wake up and race to steal tasks from Worker 0's Chase-Lev deque. What two optimizations eliminate this steal storm?

options.text: Use XorShift randomized victim ordering, cap concurrent searching thieves at cores/2, and steal half-batches in one CAS.
options.feedback: Correct! Randomized victims spread probes, searching caps limit cache traffic, and half-batch steals amortize CAS cost.

options.text: Protect all 64 deques with a single global spinlock.
options.feedback: A global spinlock reintroduces the exact contention bottleneck work-stealing avoids.

options.text: Disable work stealing and let 63 cores stay idle.
options.feedback: Disabling stealing wastes 98% of CPU capacity on unbalanced workloads.

options.text: Spin all 63 cores in a tight while(true) loop.
options.feedback: Busy spinning burns 100% power and starves the active core via thermal/memory contention.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Randomized victim probes, searching-thread caps, and half-batch stealing eliminate cross-core steal storms.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must `top` and `bottom` indices inside a Chase-Lev deque be padded to separate 64-byte cache lines?

options.text: To eliminate false sharing so the owner's frequent Bottom updates don't invalidate thieves' cached reads of Top (and vice versa).
options.feedback: Correct! Cache-line padding prevents MESI invalidation ping-ponging between owner and thieves.

options.text: Because 64-bit integers require 64-byte alignment on x86.
options.feedback: 64-bit integers only require 8-byte alignment; 64 bytes is the CPU L1 cache-line size.

options.text: To fit 64 tasks inside a single integer.
options.feedback: Padding separates two metadata indices across cache lines.

options.text: To allow Python's GIL to run in parallel.
options.feedback: Cache-line padding is a hardware MESI optimization for native multi-core threads.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Separating top and bottom onto distinct 64-byte cache lines prevents hardware false sharing.

knowledgeChecks.question: A monitoring dashboard shows `runtime_task_poll_duration_p99_us` jumping from 35 us to 45,000 us (45 ms), causing p99 API latency to spike across unrelated endpoints. What is the most likely root cause?

options.text: An async task is executing a synchronous blocking call (like file I/O, DNS, or a std::sync::Mutex) directly on a worker thread instead of using `spawn_blocking`.
options.feedback: Correct! Blocking an async worker thread stalls all other tasks queued on that core until the syscall returns.

options.text: The 128-poll cooperative budget is too small.
options.feedback: A smaller budget yields faster, keeping individual poll durations shorter—not 45 ms.

options.text: Idle workers are parked on epoll.
options.feedback: Parked idle workers wake up in microseconds and do not inflate active poll duration.

options.text: The global queue is checked every 61 ticks.
options.feedback: A global queue try_pop() takes nanoseconds.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Multi-millisecond poll() durations indicate synchronous blocking calls stalling the async worker thread.

beginner.summary: A multi-core async runtime gives each CPU core its own task queue, steals work in batches when idle, and moves slow blocking calls to a separate pool.
beginner.keyTakeaway: Run one worker per core, steal work when idle, and never block async worker threads with slow disk or network calls.
beginner.byteSummary: To run 500,000 tasks across 64 CPU cores, give each core its own fast queue, let idle cores borrow half of a busy core's queue, and isolate slow blocking work onto backup threads.

intermediate.summary: Combine a 20 ns LIFO fast-slot, 64-byte-padded 256-slot Chase-Lev deques, 61-tick global fairness, and randomized half-batch stealing.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: Use MPSC global injection queues, NUMA-local victim preference, and epoll/io_uring parking when all queues are empty.
